IC1.name: Cybercrime Offender Focus
IC1.definition: The study investigates individuals who commit cybercriminal acts, treating offenders as the primary subject rather than only technical threats.
IC1.signals: cybercriminal, cyber offender, hacker, malicious insider, online fraudster, cybercrime perpetrator, dark web vendor
IC1.negative_indicators: cybersecurity defense, network intrusion, malware detection, cyber victimization

IC2.name: Profiling Activity
IC2.definition: The study aims to infer, classify, or predict offender characteristics (e.g., demographics, personality, location, technical skill) from digital evidence, online behavior, or textual data.
IC2.signals: profiling, behavioral profiling, psychological profiling, attribution, stylometry, authorship analysis, personality prediction, classification of offenders
IC2.negative_indicators: associating malware to a specific attacker group through threat intelligence, IP tracking, generic anomaly detection

IC3.name: Human Factors Emphasis
IC3.definition: The study explicitly incorporates psychological, sociological, cognitive, or motivational concepts to explain or model offender behavior.
IC3.signals: motivation, personality traits, psychopathy, cognitive bias, human factors, social engineering, cyberpsychology, behavioral theory, self-control, moral disengagement
IC3.negative_indicators: technical skill measurement, cryptographic expertise, code obfuscation techniques

IC4.name: Empirical or Methodological Contribution
IC4.definition: The study provides original empirical data (e.g., experiments, surveys, case series, datasets) or formulates/validates a novel method, framework, or algorithm for profiling, or systematically reviews existing evidence.
IC4.signals: empirical, case study, survey, interviews, experiment, dataset, machine learning model, predictive model, framework, systematic review, meta-analysis
IC4.negative_indicators: editorial, opinion, tutorial, purely descriptive technical report without a method or systematic data collection
